assumptions: The responder cannot run code, open the app, or see a live screen; anything needing those is unknown, not guessed.
The operator sends this job to a fresh ChatGPT conversation in a new tab; the job therefore carries its own complete context.
Implementation of the roadmap happens afterwards in separate calls; this job designs only and changes no product file.
constraints: The four owner reports are claims to verify with file and line evidence, not confirmed findings; the roadmap may disagree with any of them given evidence.
No code or lesson rewrites; roadmap and adjudication only.
No roles or permission-system design; the operator deferred that work.
Do not relitigate settled architecture (server-side practice copy, undo inside the lesson, admin-only for now) except where a reported flaw directly implicates it.

deliverables.description: Adjudication of each owner report with evidence, the defect survey, the single sequenced roadmap (goal, acceptance criteria, verification method, effort per item), the proposed partition into independent verifiable follow-up work packages with their order, and the unknowns list.

facts: Piece 9 rebuilt the Net Exchange tutorial: a lesson engine plus 15 lessons under app/src/web/tutorial/lessons/, a server-side practice copy as sandbox, undo-inside-the-lesson, a tour ceiling of 8 steps and a practice ceiling of 16 steps (18 allowed for sending money).
The operator walked every lesson as administrator with all access on his own running copy. His verdict: the scaffolding proves doable but is not acceptable and is full of flaws.
His four walkthrough reports plus the overall mandate are quoted verbatim in owner-oracle-brief.md; an earlier commission-wording note is in verdicts.md.
Standing operator decisions: admin-only for now; the Operator role and a permission system come later on his word; no product file was changed during the walkthrough.
history-meta-review.md, history-meta-corrections.md and history-prep-notes.md record what an earlier review already found and fixed.
hypotheses: The Back-button fault may involve an interplay between lesson-step state and panel navigation rather than one wrong line.
The visual defects may cluster in a few layout causes rather than being scattered one-offs.
purpose: Give the operator one authoritative roadmap from the proven-but-flawed tutorial scaffolding to a flawless learning system.

acceptance.condition: Report 1 (Back during an undo: bugged out, undid earlier work, stuck) carries an explicit verdict of reproduces, partially reproduces, cannot reproduce from the package, or not a defect, each with file and line evidence.

requirements.requirement: ADJUDICATE REPORT 1. Verify the Back-button report against the lesson engine (tutorial-engine-Tutorial.tsx, tutorial-lessons.ts, tutorial-place.ts) and the affected lessons. Quote the exact lines that support the verdict.

acceptance.condition: Report 2 (lessons demand too little; currencies never changed; demand for maximal learner effort) carries an explicit verdict per claim with file and line evidence, counting which steps across the fifteen lessons require real input versus pressing Enter.

requirements.requirement: ADJUDICATE REPORT 2. Verify the minimal-demand report against all fifteen lesson files and the step members in tutorial-lessons.ts and history-prep-notes.md. State plainly where the report holds and where it does not.

acceptance.condition: Report 3 (safety checks undermined; operator checks one section, not whole deal details) carries an explicit verdict with file and line evidence from the lessons that touch deal approval, reverting, and payouts.

requirements.requirement: ADJUDICATE REPORT 3. Verify the safety-coverage report against the lessons, the practice-copy behaviour visible in the sources, and the lesson tests. Name what is actually checked in each safety-relevant lesson step.

acceptance.condition: Report 4 (many visual defects, learner's view) is answered with a concrete list grounded in the engine's card/panel markup and the lessons, each item located; items needing a live screen are marked unknown, not asserted.

requirements.requirement: ADJUDICATE REPORT 4. Survey the tutorial presentation code and the fifteen lessons for visual and wording defects a learner would meet. Include the earlier commission-summary note from verdicts.md in this survey.

acceptance.condition: The survey lists every further defect with evidence, location, and severity, across function, pedagogical coverage, sandbox behaviour as visible in code, and test blind spots; absence of further defects in an area is stated, not implied.

requirements.requirement: SURVEY BEYOND THE FOUR REPORTS. Report any further defects of any kind in the engine, the lessons, the practice books, and the lesson tests (tests-tutorial.test.ts, tests-lesson-figures.ts).

acceptance.condition: The roadmap is one sequence; every item has a goal, observable acceptance criteria, a verification method executable locally, and a rough effort size; the least-steps versus maximal-effort tension is resolved with a stated rule or escalated as an explicit operator decision.

requirements.requirement: WRITE THE ROADMAP. Produce the single sequenced roadmap from the current scaffolding to a flawless tutorial. Propose whatever sequence the evidence supports; no phase count or structure is prescribed.

acceptance.condition: The partition lists work packages that can each be built and verified on their own, with their required order and the reason for it.

requirements.requirement: PARTITION THE EXECUTION. Propose how the roadmap's execution splits into independent, parallelisable follow-up work packages and the order they must run in. Propose whatever partition the evidence supports.

acceptance.condition: Every point the package cannot settle (live screen, real printer, narrow windows, matters of taste) is listed with the exact evidence that would settle it; nothing is guessed.

requirements.requirement: LIST THE UNKNOWNS. State what cannot be decided from the package and what would settle each point.

acceptance.condition: Where evidence is missing the response uses PARTIAL or BLOCKED for the affected requirement with explicit limitations; no live-screen or run-code claims appear anywhere.

requirements.requirement: STAY HONEST. Mark gaps PARTIAL or BLOCKED with explicit limitations instead of inventing content.

in: Verification of each owner report against the supplied sources
A defect survey across engine, lessons, sandbox behaviour as visible in code, and tests
One sequenced roadmap with acceptance criteria, verification methods, and effort sizes
A proposed partition of the execution into independent verifiable work packages plus their order
out: Any claim requiring running code, a live screen, or a real printer
Relitigating settled architecture except where a reported flaw implicates it

sources.role: The operator's verbatim walkthrough reports and standing decisions; the assignment's highest authority.
Earlier walkthrough note on commission wording in deal summaries.
The lesson engine: cards, Back/Next behaviour, key handling, practice sandbox wiring.
Lesson list, step members, and step-resolution logic the lessons build on.
How lesson steps anchor to panel parts.
Practice-customer and practice-copy client behaviour during lessons.
Fixed practice books every lesson runs on.
Deal panels the core lessons drive, including the deal summary lines.
Receipt display of give, commission, and total for comparison with panel summaries.
Specified behaviour, including the tutorial section and the panel table.
Design background, including the tutorial section.
History: what the earlier design review corrected; background only.
History: the earlier design review itself; background only.
History: step members and practice-book notes from the preparing call.
Lesson engine and anchor tests; the contract the lessons must keep.

stop_condition: Stop when roadmap.md and the main JSON are delivered. Deliver COMPLETE only if every requirement is MET with its evidence; otherwise PARTIAL or BLOCKED with explicit limitations.
task: Adjudicate the operator's four walkthrough reports against the supplied tutorial code, survey for further defects, and write the single sequenced roadmap to a flawless tutorial with a partitioned execution plan.
title: Net Exchange tutorial oracle: roadmap to flawless
